operators.notes: Scan the dense part array (2M entries), collect partkeys matching brand+container into a flat vector. ~1/25 brands * 1/40 containers ≈ 0.1%.

For each qualifying partkey, use the grouped index (offsets+row_ids) to gather l_quantity and l_extendedprice. ~30 rows per partkey * ~2000 partkeys = ~60K rows. Rows are naturally grouped by partkey from the index structure.

Since index groups rows by partkey, process each group independently: first pass computes avg, second pass filters and sums. Each group is ~30 rows so both passes are cache-local. Materialize l_quantity and l_extendedprice per group in a small buffer (~480 bytes per group).

data_structures.partial_sums: thread_local double accumulator, reduce at end

parallelism.description: Partition ~2000 qualifying partkeys evenly across threads. Each thread processes its partkeys independently using the index — no synchronization needed during computation. Final reduction sums per-thread accumulators.
parallelism.notes: Only 16 threads despite 64 cores: the work is small (~60K rows total) and HDD random reads from the index are the bottleneck. More threads would cause disk seek thrashing.

notes: Q17 uses index-based access (NOT the shared scan_lineitem_full) because only ~0.1% of parts qualify, making indexed gather (~60K rows) vastly cheaper than scanning 60M rows. The correlated subquery is decorrelated into per-partkey two-phase processing, leveraging the natural grouping from lineitem_partkey_grouped index.
